$comment: Tile headlines and ledes for the Atlas cards (owner points 1, 15, 16, 18 Oct 2026). Each line restates only what its cited rows say: a place title comes from its own sheet's 'why' row, a region or Spain line from the places listed in 'from'. Draft until the owner OKs it. Batch 1 Portugal tile lines (24 places, 6 regions, 22 Oct 2026) are draft, drafted from each sheet's why row; owner rewrites. Germany tile lines (Mosel, Rheingau, 23 Oct 2026) are draft, drafted from each fact sheet; owner rewrites. Austria tile lines (Wachau, Neusiedlersee, 23 Oct 2026) are draft, drafted from the DAC regulations (BGBl. II 200/2020, 431/2020) before the fact sheets exist, so they cite nothing yet; owner rewrites.

spain.lede: From Atlantic rain in the north to volcanic ash in the Canaries. Pick a region and fly in.

green-spain.title: Spain's green north
green-spain.lede: On the Atlantic coast the climate is mild and humid, with about 1,600 mm of rain at Getaria. Inland Galicia turns drier and hotter.

castilla-y-leon.title: High, harsh and continental
castilla-y-leon.lede: A high plateau with hard winters and big swings between day and night. In Ribera del Duero, Tempranillo is made to age.

rioja.title: Where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean
rioja.lede: Two climates meet here, with about 400 mm of rain. The reds are made for ageing.

ebro.title: Shaped by the cierzo
ebro.lede: A dry wind, the cierzo, keeps the vines short of water. They ripen slowly, into deep-coloured, aromatic wines.

cataluna.title: From the sea to the mountains
cataluna.lede: Vines from the coast, shaped by the sea, to mountain slopes sheltered from it. Priorat's steep slate gives deep-coloured reds.

mediterranean.title: Monastrell country
mediterranean.lede: Hot, dry and limy. Monastrell gives broad, fleshy reds here.

meseta.title: Wide, dry plains under strong sun
meseta.lede: Plains with 300 to 350 mm of rain and 3,000 hours of sun. Low yields add balance.

andalucia.title: Flor and the solera
andalucia.lede: In Jerez, flor yeast and soleras age the wines. The vines grow on albariza, a soft marl that holds moisture.

baleares.title: Island vines at sea level
baleares.lede: Island vineyards at sea level, under strong sun. The salty Embat wind keeps them cool.

canarias.title: Native grapes on volcanic soil
canarias.lede: Native grapes on volcanic soil, under an Atlantic climate. On Lanzarote they grow in ash behind stone walls, on 150 mm of rain.

pt-north.title: Granite by the sea, schist inland
pt-north.lede: Vinho Verde takes the Atlantic rain on granite. Behind the Marão, the Douro sits on schist, out of the wet west winds.

pt-centre.title: Granite, clay and a nearby sea
pt-centre.lede: Dão is granite ringed by mountains. Bairrada is clay hills with a strong Atlantic influence.

pt-lisboa.title: The Atlantic coast north of the Tejo
pt-lisboa.lede: A coastal strip with humid west winds and dry summers. Colares grows its vines in sand close to the sea.

pt-tejo.title: Plains and heath beside the Tagus
pt-tejo.lede: Flat alluvial plains, clay-limestone hills and sandy heath soils. About 2,800 hours of sun a year.

pt-setubal.title: Sand between two estuaries
pt-setubal.lede: Light, sandy soils on a peninsula between the Tejo and Sado estuaries, with little rain.

pt-alentejo.title: Flat, sunny and hot
pt-alentejo.lede: About 3,000 sun hours a year and hot, dry summers, on soils from limestone to granite.

pt-algarve.title: A hot south coast behind mountains
pt-algarve.lede: A dry, sunny Mediterranean coast, sheltered from cold northern winds by mountains, on poor sandy soils.

pt-madeira.title: Volcanic islands in the Atlantic
pt-madeira.lede: Steep terraces on basalt, with mild temperatures while the grapes ripen.

fr-burgundy.title: Limestone slopes, frost in spring
fr-burgundy.lede: Chablis sits on limestone and marl. Frost in winter and spring is a fairly serious risk.

fr-bordeaux.title: Gravel terraces by the estuary
fr-bordeaux.lede: Pauillac's gravel drains well. The Atlantic and the Gironde soften the climate.

fr-loire.title: Schist, chalk and flint along the river
fr-loire.lede: Anjou has schist in the west and tuffeau chalk in the east. Sancerre's steep hills carry marl, limestone and flint.

fr-rhone.title: Granite in the north, pebbles in the south
fr-rhone.lede: Hermitage is a granite hill facing the sun. Châteauneuf-du-Pape's pebbles store the day's heat.

fr-south-west.title: Valleys between the Atlantic and the Pyrenees
fr-south-west.lede: Cahors sits on limestone plateaus by the Lot. Madiran's foothills ripen late Tannat.

fr-beaujolais.title: Granite slopes for Gamay
fr-beaujolais.lede: Fleurie's poor pink granite sands give light, scented reds. Moulin-à-Vent's granite carries manganese.

fr-alsace.title: Dry and sunny behind the Vosges
fr-alsace.lede: The Vosges hold off the rain. Hot days and cool nights suit many aromatic grapes.

fr-south.title: Heat, wind and stony ground
fr-south.lede: Hot, dry summers ration water. Bandol's sea air lets late Mourvèdre ripen.

fr-champagne.title: Chalk and natural acidity
fr-champagne.lede: Chalk, marl or sand slopes drain naturally. The climate keeps the acidity sparkling wine needs.

it-piemonte.title: Marl hills of the Langhe
it-piemonte.lede: Barolo grows on calcareous marl and clay. Only hillsides between 170 and 540 m qualify.

it-tuscany.title: Galestro, sandstone, hot dry summers
it-tuscany.lede: Chianti Classico's hills are shale and sandstone. Summers are dry and often above 35 °C.

it-lombardia.title: Glacial moraine and steep terraces
it-lombardia.lede: Franciacorta sits on glacial moraine beside Lake Iseo. Valtellina grows on steep dry-stone granite terraces.

it-north-east.title: Alpine valleys and stony gravel
it-north-east.lede: Alto Adige's valleys are sunny with big day-night swings. Friuli Grave sits on stony river gravel.

it-veneto.title: Volcanic hills and alluvial plains
it-veneto.lede: Soave grows on volcanic basalt and limestone. Prosecco covers mostly flat alluvial plain with some hills.

it-emilia-romagna.title: Clay and limestone foothills
it-emilia-romagna.lede: Pignoletto grows on clay and limy foothills. Albana sits on clay and limestone hills.

it-centre.title: Volcanic tuff and Adriatic hills
it-centre.lede: Orvieto's hills are volcanic tuff over clay and sand. Abruzzo's Adriatic hills are loose, well-drained clay-sand.

it-south.title: Inland hills and a limestone plateau
it-south.lede: Taurasi grows on inland clay and limestone hills with big day-night swings. Castel del Monte is a stony limestone plateau.

it-islands.title: Volcanic slopes and sandy granite
it-islands.lede: Etna's slopes are loose volcanic soil. Gallura in Sardinia has sandy granite and salty wind.

de-mosel.title: Riesling above a winding river
de-mosel.lede: Half the vineyards face south-east to south-west. They lie between 65 and 375 m.

de-rheingau.title: Riesling on the Rhine's sunny slopes
de-rheingau.lede: Riesling covers about 80% of the vineyards. The Taunus forests slow the cold night air.

at-wachau.title: Riesling and Grüner Veltliner above the Danube
at-wachau.lede: A Ried wine may only be Grüner Veltliner or Riesling. The Ried is named with its village.

at-neusiedlersee.title: Zweigelt around a shallow lake
at-neusiedlersee.lede: The area is a whole district, minus two villages. The red DAC wine is Zweigelt.
